name: Mawrth Vallis Layered Clays

resources.detail: Fe/Mg clays (nontronite) at stratigraphic base, overlain by Al-clays (kaolinite) and hydrated silica.
Ferrous-iron bearing hydrated phases identified by CRISM orbital spectroscopy.

surfaceFacts.label: Clay Stratigraphy
surfaceFacts.value: Fe/Mg smectite base under Al-rich clays

summary: Spectacular ancient outflow channel exposing one of the thickest sequences of phyllosilicate clays on Mars.

sources.title: NASA Planetary Data System Phyllosilicate Catalog

name: CRISM Crater Floor & Wall Target

resources.detail: Iron-magnesium phyllosilicate clays exposed along crater wall terraces.
Unaltered olivine-rich basaltic floor unit.

summary: Targeted CRISM spectrometer site resolving excavated deep-seated crustal smectites and olivine sandstones.

name: CRISM Escarpment Slope Target (Nili Fossae Margin)

resources.detail: Fe-Mg smectite clays and aluminum-rich clays along fault scarp.
Crystalline olivine bedrock exposed by tectonic graben extension.

summary: Prominent fault scarp in the Nili Fossae / Syrtis Major transition zone exposing layered clays and unaltered olivine.

name: Gusev Crater Basaltic Plains (Adirondack Class)

resources.detail: Unaltered olivine basalt: plagioclase 39%, olivine 20%, low-Ca pyroxene 15%, augite 15%.

summary: Spirit rover exploration plains proving the unaltered volcanic nature of Gusev Crater floor basalt lavas.

sources.title: NASA Mars Exploration Rover Spirit Mineralogy

name: Columbia Hills Hydrothermal Alteration (Clovis & Paso Robles)

resources.detail: Goethite up to 40% of total iron in Clovis rock class (direct evidence of ancient liquid water).
Ferric sulfate enriched soil (~65% of iron as Fe3+-sulfate) discovered in Paso Robles churned soil.

summary: Columbia Hills formations where Spirit discovered compelling mineral evidence of acidic hydrothermal spring activity.

sources.title: Spirit Rover Science Results: Columbia Hills

name: Meridiani Planum Hematite Plains

resources.detail: Gray crystalline hematite up to 20 wt% (orbital TES detection); millimeter-scale hematite spherules ("blueberries").
Jarosite and calcium/magnesium sulfate hydrated salts cementing basaltic sandstone.

summary: Opportunity rover landing plain demonstrating sustained groundwater percolation through jarosite and hematite spherules.

name: Rocknest Eolian Bedform (Gale Crater)

resources.detail: Soil ~55 wt% crystalline basaltic (plagioclase 22.3%, olivine 12.3%, augite 8.0%, pigeonite 7.6%, magnetite 1.2%, anhydrite 0.8%).
X-ray amorphous phase (~45 wt%) acting as principal host for volatile H2O, SO2, CO2, O2, and Cl.

summary: Curiosity first scoop sample analysis site revealing the detailed volatile and mineral composition of global Martian drift dust.

name: Octavia E. Butler Landing Site (Jezero Crater)

resources.detail: River delta bottomset mudstones containing smectite clays preserving organic molecules.
Feedstock processed by MOXIE instrument to produce breathable oxygen at ~6 g/hour rate.

summary: Operational landing site of the Perseverance rover and Ingenuity helicopter in western Jezero Crater.

name: Bradbury Landing (Gale Crater)

resources.detail: Yellowknife Bay Sheepbed mudstone clay units formed in habitable ancient freshwater lake.
Calcium sulfate mineral veins (gypsum/bassanite) cross-cutting fractured bedrock.

summary: Curiosity rover touchdown site on the gravel-paved northern floor of Gale Crater near Mount Sharp.

name: Eagle Crater Landing Site (Meridiani Planum)

resources.detail: Gray hematite spherules eroding out of sulfate-rich outcrop layers.

summary: First touchdown crater of Opportunity, discovering outcrop bedrock confirming ancient groundwater.

name: Columbia Memorial Station (Gusev Crater)

resources.detail: Olivine basalt floor boulders with thin eolian dust coatings.

summary: Spirit rover touchdown station in southern Gusev Crater, dedicated to the crew of Space Shuttle Columbia.

name: Thomas Mutch Memorial Station (Viking 1 Lander)

resources.detail: Iron-rich silicates and titanomagnetite in Chryse Planitia rocky regolith.

summary: First operational soft landing on Mars (20 July 1976), confirming red iron oxide soils and atmospheric pressure.

name: Utopia Planitia Station (Viking 2 Lander)

resources.detail: Observed thin seasonal water-ice frost coatings during Martian winter.

summary: High-latitude northern plains landing site surrounded by polygonal frost fractures and angular boulders.

name: Phoenix Green Valley (Northern Arctic Plains)

resources.detail: Pure subsurface water ice directly excavated under lander thrusters and in "Snow White" trench (vaporized into TEGA).
Calcium carbonate and alkaline soil chemistry detected by wet chemistry laboratory.

summary: MEASURED ground-truth water-ice site. Phoenix confirmed massive pure water ice centimeters beneath arctic permafrost.

sources.title: NASA Phoenix Mars Lander Science Archive

name: InSight Elysium Planitia Seismic Outpost

resources.detail: Homogeneous loose regolith optimal for thermal probe penetration and seismometer coupling.

summary: Geophysical observatory that recorded over 1,300 marsquakes, defining the crustal thickness and liquid metallic core of Mars.

name: Carl Sagan Memorial Station (Mars Pathfinder & Sojourner)

resources.detail: Silica-rich andesitic rocks ("Barnacle Bill") and volcanic basalts ("Yogi") in catastrophic flood deposits.

summary: Airbag-assisted landing site in ancient outflow channel Ares Vallis; deployed the first extraterrestrial rover Sojourner.

name: Arcadia Planitia Subsurface Ice Zone (SWIM)

resources.detail: Shallow subsurface water-ice sheets (within 1 to 2.5 m of surface) mapped by SWIM multi-dataset fusion (radar, thermal, neutron).

summary: Prime In-Situ Resource Utilization (ISRU) water extraction target. Flat plains with shallow buried glacier-like sheets.

name: Acidalia Planitia Subsurface Ice Zone (SWIM)

resources.detail: Subsurface permafrost and ground ice mapped by SHARAD radar dielectric permittivity reflections.

summary: Extensive low-elevation northern basin holding radar-detected subsurface ice reserves beneath protective regolith.

name: Deuteronilus Mensae Debris-Covered Glaciers

resources.detail: Lobate Debris Aprons (LDAs) confirmed by SHARAD radar to be massive water-ice glaciers (>90% ice) under tens of meters of rock debris.

summary: Freckled mesa terrain hosting extensive debris-covered glaciers preserved from Mars high-obliquity ice ages.

sources.title: SHARAD Radar Glaciology at Deuteronilus Mensae

name: Utopia Planitia Subsurface Ice Sheet

resources.detail: Enormous subsurface ice deposit estimated to hold volume of water equivalent to Lake Superior (SHARAD radar findings).

summary: Vast northern impact basin concealing thick sheets of water ice underneath 1 to 10 meters of surface soil.

sources.title: NASA SHARAD Utopia Planitia Ice Discovery

name: Planum Boreum (North Polar Layered Ice Deposits)

resources.detail: Massive continuous polar cap consisting of pure water ice layered with atmospheric dust (thickness up to 3 km).

summary: The largest surface water reservoir on Mars, holding approximately 1.6 million cubic kilometers of water ice.

sources.title: NASA Planetary Photojournal North Polar Cap

name: Planum Australe (South Polar Residual Ice Cap)

resources.detail: Base water-ice layered deposits capped by an 8-meter perennial veneer of dry ice (solid carbon dioxide).

summary: South polar ice sheet combining permanent water ice layers with active seasonal carbon dioxide dry-ice sublimation cycles.

name: Korolev Crater Permanent Water-Ice Dome

resources.detail: 81-km-wide impact crater filled with a 1.8-km-thick permanent mound of water ice trapped by cold-trap atmospheric microclimate.

summary: Spectacular ice-filled crater near the north polar cap imaged extensively by ESA Mars Express High Resolution Stereo Camera.

sources.title: ESA Mars Express Korolev Crater Ice Mound

name: Nili Fossae Carbonate & Serpentine Fractures

resources.detail: Magnesite (Mg-carbonate) deposits formed by low-temperature hydrothermal alteration of ultramafic olivine rocks.
Serpentine mineral phases indicating serpentinization reactions capable of generating hydrogen and methane.

summary: Fractured graben system preserving carbonate and serpentine minerals critical for understanding ancient Martian habitability.

sources.title: CRISM Carbonate Discovery in Nili Fossae

name: Syrtis Major Planum Basaltic Shield

resources.detail: Unweathered tholeiitic basalt bedrock and dacite-bearing volcanic flows around Nili Patera caldera.

summary: Low-relief volcanic shield of Hesperian age displaying prominent dark wind streaks of unweathered pyroxene-rich sand.

name: Jezero Crater Western Fan Delta Escarpment

resources.detail: Finely laminated bottomset mudstones enriched in smectites and detrital carbonates.

summary: Ancient river delta front in Jezero where ancient microbial biosignatures are actively cored and cached by Perseverance.

name: Comanche Outcrop (Columbia Hills)

resources.detail: High concentration of magnesium-iron carbonate (16 to 34 wt%) discovered by Spirit Mossbauer and Mini-TES spectrometers.

summary: Definitive in-situ detection of substantial carbonate minerals, demonstrating near-neutral aqueous alteration on early Mars.

name: Egg Rock Iron-Nickel Meteorite

resources.detail: Deeply grooved iron-nickel meteorite composed of kamacite and taenite metal alloys, verified by ChemCam laser spectroscopy.

summary: Golf-ball sized iron-nickel metallic meteorite discovered by Curiosity in Gale Crater, preserved with negligible oxidation.

sources.title: Curiosity ChemCam Laser Analysis of Egg Rock

name: Finger-Like Cemented Diagenetic Concretions

resources.detail: Sulfate and silica cementation along ancient fracture networks eroded into delicate protruding fingers.

summary: Curiosity Mastcam finding illustrating differential diagenetic cementation by groundwater fluids in ancient lake sediments.

sources.title: Curiosity Views Delicate Rock Fingers in Gale Crater

name: Yellowknife Bay (John Klein & Cumberland Sample Sites)

resources.detail: Saponite smectite clays drilled from Sheepbed mudstone; established ancient neutral pH fresh water lake.

summary: Site of Curiosity first drilled rock powders, confirming habitability (C, H, N, O, P, S bio-essential elements present).

sources.title: Curiosity Habitability Findings at Yellowknife Bay

name: Olympus Mons Summit Caldera Complex

resources.detail: Tholeiitic basalt lava flows and extensive uncollapsed lava tube systems.

summary: The tallest shield volcano in the solar system, crowned with six nested pit calderas spanning 80 km across.

name: Hellas Planitia Basin Floor

resources.detail: Highest atmospheric surface pressure on Mars (~12.4 mbar at -7,152 m datum depth), mitigating UV/radiation exposure.

summary: Deepest impact basin on Mars (over 7 km deep), occasionally thick enough to allow temporary liquid water stability under peak temperatures.

name: Melas Chasma (Valles Marineris Floor)

resources.detail: Thick Light-Toned Deposits (LTDs) of kieserite and polyhydrated sulfates spanning canyon floor.

summary: Central and widest abyss of the Valles Marineris grand canyon system, plunging 9 km below adjacent plateau plains.

sources.title: CRISM Hydrated Sulfate Mapping in Melas Chasma

name: Jezero Delta Front Escarpment

hazards.label: Steep Escarpment & Rockfall
hazards.detail: Steep 24.5° talus cliff with loose boulders and unstable slope faces separating delta from crater floor.

summary: Steep erosional cliff and boulder-strewn talus slopes separating the delta fan top from the crater floor. Bypass via designated ramp.

name: Kodiak Butte Perimeter Precipice

hazards.label: Sub-Vertical Mesa Cliff
hazards.detail: Sub-vertical cliff face (slope 36.0°) around Kodiak remnant mesa. Severe fall hazard.

summary: Strict exclusion zone. Keep EVA traverses at least 300 meters away from base to avoid catastrophic rockfall.

sources.title: Mastcam-Z Stereo Imagery of Kodiak Butte

name: Bagnold Dunes Field (Gale Crater)

resources.detail: Fine unbonded basaltic sand dunes with loose grain packing.

hazards.label: Active Dune Mobility Trap
hazards.detail: Barchan dunes with slip faces exceeding 30 degrees; extreme wheel entrapment and boot sinkage hazard.

summary: Active dark barchan dune field across the path to Mount Sharp. Traverse only at designated bedrock crossing points.

name: Olympus Mons Basal Scarp Ring

hazards.label: 6-8 km Sheer Basal Scarp
hazards.detail: Immense cliff ring surrounding the volcano base dropping 6 to 8 vertical kilometers on 45° slopes.

summary: Completely impassable for ground travel. Aerial ascent or orbital transport mandatory.

name: Coprates Chasma Wall Precipices

hazards.label: 8 km Vertical Canyon Drop
hazards.detail: Massive landslide scarps dropping 8,000 meters into canyon abyss on slopes exceeding 35 degrees.

summary: Deepest chasma cliffs of Valles Marineris. Impassable for rover transit.

name: Palikir Crater Recurring Slope Lineae (RSL)

hazards.label: Steep Granular Avalanche Hazard (RSL)
hazards.detail: NASA/HiRISE confirms RSL occur on slopes >27° matching dry angle of repose. Dry/granular sand cascades, NOT a water resource. Water status: CONTESTED.

summary: SCIENTIFIC GUARDRAIL: Recurring slope lineae are dry granular flows on steep unstable crater walls. Never classify as water resources.

sources.title: NASA/USGS HiRISE RSL Granular Flow Findings

name: Hale Crater Central Peak RSL Complex

hazards.label: Steep Slump & Granular Cascades (RSL)
hazards.detail: Dark narrow streaks on 28°–34° central peak slopes representing granular flows. Contested planetary science site; impassable terrain.

summary: NASA HiRISE monitored site of active seasonal slope flows on steep terrain. Strictly treated as mobility hazard.

sources.title: HiRISE Investigation of Hale Crater Slope Features

name: Gusev Dust Devil High-Frequency Alley

hazards.label: Electrostatic Dust Whirlwinds
hazards.detail: High concentration of active daytime convective vortices carrying abrasive electrostatic dust plumes.

summary: Corridor characterized by numerous dust devils documented by Spirit rover, causing solar panel scrub/dusting and electrostatic hazards.

sources.title: Spirit Navcam Dust Devil Movie Archive

name: Planetary Ambient Atmosphere (Oxygen Feedstock)

resources.detail: Mars global atmosphere (95.32% CO2, 1.6% N2, 1.9% Ar). Feedstock for Solid Oxide Electrolysis (MOXIE) to generate O2 and CO.

summary: Global planetary atmosphere. Accessible everywhere on the Martian surface as an In-Situ Resource Utilization (ISRU) life support feedstock.
